Double Hovered Stack (assign a hotkey; hover a slot and press it)
cheats.enableScript:
-- Doubles the stack in the inventory slot under the mouse, past the max stack.
-- Chain (Schedule I): ItemUIManager.HoveredSlot(+0x30) -> ItemSlotUI.assignedSlot(+0x28)
--   -> ItemSlot.ItemInstance(+0x10) -> ItemInstance.Quantity(+0x10, int32).
local mgr = tonumber(state.mgr)
if not mgr or mgr == 0 then
  error("Inventory UI not captured yet: open your inventory, move the mouse, and try again.")
end
local ui = readInt64(mgr + 0x30)
if ui == 0 then error("Hover an item slot first.") end
local slot = readInt64(ui + 0x28)
if slot == 0 then error("That slot is not assigned.") end
local inst = readInt64(slot + 0x10)
if inst == 0 then error("That slot is empty.") end
local q = readInt32(inst + 0x10)
if q < 1 or q > 1000000 then error("Unexpected quantity " .. q .. "; not touching it.") end
local doubled = q * 2
writeInt32(inst + 0x10, doubled)
print("stack " .. q .. " -> " .. doubled)

cheats.name: Instant Chemistry (batches complete on the next tick, automatically, while toggled on)
Instant Cauldron (cooks finish on the next tick)
Instant Mixing (batches complete on the next tick, automatically, while toggled on)
cheats.note: Third revision, redone the same way the oven cheat's crash got fixed. v1 force-wrote CurrentMixTime (rbx+0x220) to 999999999 every pass -- the real completion compare (`cmp ecx,edi`, edi = Quantity x MixTimePerItem freshly computed via `imul edi,[rbx+0x290]`) passed, but the 'mins remaining' label reads `required - current` unclamped, so it showed an astronomically negative number ('-999999939 mins remaining', reported via screenshot). v2 instead neutralized the `imul` to `mov edi,1`, shrinking the threshold rather than forcing the progress -- this avoided the display bug, but carries the same structural risk that caused a real crash on the analogous oven fix: CurrentMixTime keeps incrementing normally with nothing to cap it, so the gap between it and an artificially tiny threshold grows unboundedly for as long as the batch sits uncollected, a plausible native/IL2CPP out-of-bounds condition if anything indexes off that ratio. Confirmed live this session: an active mix station has Quantity=20, MixTimePerItem=3 (real required-total=60), CurrentMixTime already at 69 (sitting past its real threshold, uncollected). This revision goes back to forcing CurrentMixTime itself (same instruction as v1), but to a modest, bounded 1000 instead of an astronomical constant -- comfortably above the one real required-total observed (60), pinned and re-applied every pass rather than ever-growing, and `required` is left completely untouched so its own real per-station/per-operation computation and the completion compare both run through entirely unmodified code. A batch whose real required-total exceeds 1000 would just be fast rather than instant, not unsafe. Two internal companion patches (factory-instant-mixing-display, factory-instant-mixing-complete) arm and disarm automatically with this one toggle -- see store.ts's `internal`/`companions` fields. Confirmed working live this session, all three together: progress advances, display reads 0 instead of negative, and the completion event/animation fires without needing to exit and reopen the station.

cheats.name: Instant Mixing: zero the remaining-time display
cheats.note: Companion of factory-instant-mixing (armed/disarmed together via its `companions` list; hidden from the cheat list as `internal`). Fixes Instant Mixing's '-940 mins remaining' style display, per the user's request to clamp the shown number to 0 instead of letting it go negative. Found live this session: a small standalone function (no name recovered from IL2CPP metadata -- it sits between two named methods with no MethodInfo entry of its own, likely a compiler-emitted property accessor) that does nothing but `return CurrentMixOperation.Quantity * MixTimePerItem` -- no completion check, no side effects, unlike the other 8 occurrences of this same multiply found via signature scan (all of which are inline completion checks inside MixingStation's own methods, confirmed by disassembling each). That shape -- a bare read-only total with no comparison -- is exactly what an external UI computing `remaining = total - CurrentMixTime` would call rather than recomputing the multiply itself, which is also why none of the 9 internal completion-check sites contain a subtraction: the subtraction happens in whatever external code calls this getter, not in MixingStation's own compiled code. Replaces the `imul eax,[rcx+0x290]` with `mov eax,[rcx+0x220]` (CurrentMixTime, the same object) so this getter always returns exactly whatever CurrentMixTime currently is -- any caller computing `total - current` gets exactly 0, never negative, regardless of the pinned value factory-instant-mixing forces. Confirmed via `IsMixingDone` (a separate, verified-live-uncached property) that collection availability does not depend on this getter, so overriding it should not affect whether a batch can be collected -- only the displayed number. Confirmed working live this session.

cheats.note: DryingRack.OnTimePass(minutes): xmm6 = minutes * dry multiplier is added to each DryingOperation.Time (+0x20); at Time >= DRY_MINS_PER_TIER (720) the operation gains one tier (+0x1c, Time reset to 0) and at the top tier it ends via TryEndOperation. cheats.name: Instant Ovens (cooks report complete)
cheats.note:
Fourth revision, after a crash on the third. v1 forced OvenCookOperation.IsComplete's entry to return true (froze the timer at 06:00). v2 forced only the final compare in the same method (froze it at 03:45 instead) -- proving the freeze is inherent to forcing the boolean result at all, regardless of which instruction does it. v3 (root-caused via live IL2CPP metadata -- confirmed field +0x40 is really `CookProgress` and +0x44 is really `cookDuration`, both genuine Int32 fields, not a wrong-field guess) force-cached cookDuration down to 1 -- this crashed the game (confirmed live: the process came back as a new PID with UnityCrashHandler64.exe alongside it). Read a live active cook afterward: real CookProgress=34, cookDuration=360. Forcing the duration down to a tiny constant while CookProgress keeps incrementing normally every tick means the ratio between them grows unboundedly for as long as the oven sits uncollected -- a very plausible native/IL2CPP out-of-bounds crash if anything indexes an array or animation frame off that ratio, and unlike v1/v2 this failure mode gets worse over time rather than being an immediate, bounded mistake.

This revision instead targets a different, never-before-touched site: `LabOven.OnUncappedMinPass` (found live by enumerating LabOven's real IL2CPP methods and disassembling it), which contains the actual per-tick progress increment `inc [rcx+0x40]` (rcx = the live OvenCookOperation, confirmed directly in the disassembly). Instead of incrementing CookProgress by 1 each tick, this forces it to a fixed 1000 every tick -- comfortably above the one real duration observed (360), but a modest, bounded, pinned constant rather than an ever-growing or astronomical one. cookDuration itself is left completely untouched, so its own real per-recipe lazy-init logic keeps running normally, and the completion compare (and anything reading it, including whatever the on-screen timer polls) runs through entirely unmodified code -- nothing forces a boolean, so the freeze bug (v1/v2) cannot recur, and the forced value cannot grow unbounded the way v3's did, since it is re-pinned to the same constant every pass rather than accumulating. Confirmed working in-game this session: no freeze, no crash, cook completes as intended. A recipe with a real duration above 1000 would just be fast rather than instant, not unsafe.

No ATM Deposit Limit: selected amount is never clamped to the remaining weekly allowance
No ATM Deposit Limit: the main Deposit button itself
cheats.note: Third and final gate for this wishlist item, found after both prior patches still left the deposit button disabled per live user report. ATMInterface.Update itself (not the amount-selector screen at all) directly toggles menu_DepositButton's own interactable state every frame: loads ATM.WeeklyDepositSum, compares it against the baked WeeklyDepositLimit constant (`comiss xmm8,[static_fields]; setnbe dl`, dl=1 only while sum < limit), then calls the interactable-setter with menu_DepositButton as the target. This is the button the user actually clicks FIRST, before ever reaching the amount-selector screen the other two patches cover -- once the weekly sum reaches the limit, the whole Deposit flow is locked out at the entry point regardless of what factory-atm-nodepositlimit/-clamp do downstream. Patched the local `setnbe dl` (0F 97 C2) to `mov dl,1; nop`, same technique as factory-atm-nodepositlimit. Unique 63-byte signature confirmed live via scan_aob (1 match). All three patches together should be required for a full fix: main button stays enabled (this patch) -> preset amount buttons stay enabled (factory-atm-nodepositlimit) -> the picked amount isn't zeroed back out (factory-atm-nodepositlimit-clamp). Untested in-game.

cheats.name: ATM Deposit MAX preset equals your full cash balance
cheats.note: Follow-up to the user's request: the MAX preset (index -1, ATMInterface.GetAmountFromIndex) computes min(cash-on-hand, ATMInterface.get_remainingAllowedDeposit()) -- a THIRD, independently-compiled instance of the WeeklyDepositLimit-minus-WeeklyDepositSum formula, this time behind a real named getter rather than inlined (unlike UpdateAvailableAmounts' and SetSelectedAmount's inline versions, already patched by factory-atm-nodepositlimit/-clamp). Cash-on-hand is read first (CashInstance.Balance, via the same live pointer chain factory-cash anchors), then `minss xmm6,xmm0` clamps it down to whatever remains of the weekly allowance -- so MAX showed the smaller of the two, not the player's actual total cash, even with the other three ATM patches installed (they don't touch this call site). NOPed the `minss xmm6,xmm0` (F3 0F 5D F0) so the MAX preset returns the raw cash balance unclamped; get_remainingAllowedDeposit itself is left alone since nothing else in this file calls it besides this one now-defused comparison. Unique 57-byte signature confirmed live via scan_aob (1 match). Verified live by directly calling the exact functions this code calls (call_remote_function on the object-lookup at 0x8E9690, then call_remote_function_float on the Balance getter at 0xBEAAFA0): returns 12563.5, matching the player's real cash balance read via the factory-cash pointer chain -- confirms the underlying VALUE this patch produces is correct. User still saw '-9000' after this patch -- see factory-atm-max-label-fullcash, a fourth occurrence that controls the button's own displayed text, separate from the value this patch fixes.

cheats.name: No ATM Deposit Limit: MAX button's own displayed text also uses full cash
cheats.note: Root cause of the '-9000' the user actually saw. factory-atm-max-fullcash fixed the VALUE GetAmountFromIndex(-1) computes (verified live: 12563.5, correct); this is a SEPARATE, fourth occurrence of the identical cash-vs-remainingAllowedDeposit clamp, this time inside ATMInterface.Update itself, which every frame (while depositing==true) fetches the LAST entry in amountButtons (`List.get_Item(count-1)`, i.e. the MAX button specifically), gets its Text component, and writes `min(cash, get_remainingAllowedDeposit())` into it as the button's own label -- completely independent of what GetAmountFromIndex returns when actually clicked. Since WeeklyDepositSum has grown past the old WeeklyDepositLimit(10000) thanks to the other ATM patches already letting deposits through, get_remainingAllowedDeposit() now returns a negative number (10000-19000=-9000), and min(12563.5, -9000)=-9000 -- exactly the value reported. NOPed the same `minss xmm6,xmm0` (F3 0F 5D F0) pattern so the MAX button's text also shows the raw, unclamped cash balance, matching what clicking it actually selects. Unique 61-byte signature confirmed live via scan_aob (1 match). User confirmed the label now matches cash, but reported the MAX deposit itself greyed out -- see factory-atm-max-confirm-strictfix, a genuine pre-existing game bug this exposed (not a side effect of any ATM patch).

cheats.name: ATM Deposit: allow confirming a deposit of exactly your full cash balance
cheats.note: Correction after further live investigation: xmm7 at this comparison is actually zeroed (`xorps xmm7,xmm7`) earlier in Update, not selectedAmount as first assumed -- so this gate is really just 'cash > 0', not a balance-vs-selected-amount check, and this patch (SETA->SETAE) has no real effect (balance is essentially never exactly 0).
